Options ctsem reads

Source: R/ctsem-options.R
ctsem-options.Rd

Settings that change how ctsem behaves for a whole session. Set them with options(), usually once at the top of a script or when a front end starts.

Value

Nothing. This page documents options.

Progress and output

ctsem.progress.overwrite

Whether progress reporting rewrites a single line (TRUE) or prints separate lines now and then (FALSE). If unset, ctsem decides from where the output goes. In a Shiny session, under sink() or in a knitr chunk the line is not rewritten. Set it if that choice is wrong for your front end.

ctsem.cluster.outfile

Where parallel workers send their output. If unset, they are silent. "" sends their output to the console, which is useful when debugging a worker.

Per-call alternatives

Progress and reporting can also be set for each fit, and these settings take precedence: verbose in ctFit (0 quiet, 1 reports progress, 2 keeps every progress line), optimcontrol$callback for a function called while the fit runs, and optimcontrol$progress to turn progress on or off for one fit.

Julia

The Julia backend is mostly configured through environment variables: JULIA_BINDIR names the Julia binary directory, and JULIA_NUM_THREADS the number of threads of the next session that starts. ctJuliaSetup(project=) points the session at a different engine. See ctJuliaSetup.

ctsem.julia.restart

Whether a fit asking for more cores than the running Julia session has threads may restart the session to get them. FALSE by default, because Julia fixes its number of threads when it starts, and a restart loses the code it has compiled. With FALSE, such a fit runs with the threads available and says so.
